---
title: "You check your net worth tracker more than once a day. That is not discipline."
pubDate: "2026-08-12"
draft: false
---

Joel here.

There is a spreadsheet I built in 2019 that pulled live data from my current account, my ISA, and my pension into one tab. I opened it most mornings before I opened my emails. Some days I opened it twice.

I told myself it was good financial hygiene. It was not. It was a way of taking my temperature without ever asking whether I was actually ill.

Here is what was really going on — no, wait. That framing is too tidy. Let me be more direct.

I was earning well. The number was going up. And I still felt like one bad month away from something vague and terrible. The tracker felt like evidence that the vague thing had not happened yet. Proof of safety, renewed daily.

The problem is that proof of safety is not the same as feeling safe. You can update a spreadsheet every morning for three years and still flinch when a client cancels a contract. The number does not touch the thing underneath.

This is not about the spreadsheet. Plenty of people track their finances carefully and sleep fine. The tell is the frequency and what you feel in the gap between opens. If closing the tab feels like putting down a worry stone, the number is doing a job it was never designed to do.

The question worth sitting with — and it is not a comfortable one — is this: what would need to be true about your life for the number to feel like enough?

Not "what number would be enough." That question has no answer; I have watched the target move too many times to believe it does. The question is about the life. The work. The relationships. The kind of day that leaves you tired in a way that feels earned.

I work with people who earn good money and still feel like they are failing a test they cannot see the marking scheme for. That feeling rarely lives in the spreadsheet. It lives in the story beneath the numbers — the one about what a person who earns this much is supposed to have sorted by now.

If that sentence landed somewhere specific for you, the quiz on this site takes about four minutes and will show you which money pattern is running the show. It is not a personality type. It is a behaviour under pressure. And once you can see it clearly, you can start to work with it rather than around it.

MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner
